leila: saw the alert spikes: 5xx up, 429 up, latency tail spiking. dashboards show repeated CUDA OOMs from runtime v2.3.1 on gpu-pool-eu-west.
darren: copying the alert graph — looks like rapid scale ups then scale-downs. autoscaler seems to be flapping.

(ops-bot): autoscaler-scaler: scale_up request: +6 nodes at 2024-07-12T03:12:08Z; scale_down: -5 nodes at 2024-07-12T03:12:55Z - reason: unused
tanya: that 47s churn is the problem — new nodes join, pods schedule, runtime warms KV cache and hits GPU mem boundary -> OOM -> restarts -> autoscaler thinks resources free -> scales down -> loop.
darren: agree. I'm attaching short pod logs: ```

E0724 03:12:21.124 model_server.cpp: failed to allocate KV cache for prompt
Container will exit with code 137

cs-bot: Notifying CS rotation: incident affecting inference latency and errors for Hosted customers in eu-west.

darren: do it — we'll lose some elasticity but stop crashlooping. I can patch HPA/CA flags.

cs-bot: advising CS rotation: outage window ~03:12-03:28 UTC, partial impact, some 502s and increased latency. pushing to affected customers.
mike: root cause hypothesis for postmortem: aggressive scale-down window on autoscaler combined with runtime memory growth during warmups -> transient oversubscription -> CUDA OOM -> pod restarts -> autoscaler treats pods as free resources -> rapid downscale -> repeat. Also driver version mismatch on some older nodes increased failure rate.
darren: found cluster-autoscaler logs showing `scaleDownUnneeded` toggling due to transient low allocatable gpu usage. we need longer stabilization window and a cooldown on scale-down.
leila: immediate follow-ups for next 24h: 1) keep autoscaler disabled for eu-west until we deploy corrected config. 2) force new node image with updated GPU driver on rotation. 3) add conservative KV cache sizing as default for runtime variants serving small-batch workloads. 4) update scale-down delay to 10m.
sre-oncall: adding to incident board and linking runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/inference-autoscale-oom — please add any command snippets you ran.
mike: adding snippet I used to reproduce locally and verify fix: ```bash
# simulate burst and prevent immediate scale-down
kubectl annotate deployment inference-runtime-eu autoscaler.redwood/scale-down-disabled=true -n inference
kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-runtime-eu -n inference
```
